In 13 Leaves, players can play one or more cards of the same value that align with the sequence on the table. The cards must be of a value equal to or lower than the lowest card in the sequence, or of a value equal to or higher than the highest card in the sequence. The game consists of several rounds. Each round is divided into turns that proceed clockwise. On their turn, the active player, if they can and if they want, plays one or more cards of the same value from their hand. Multiple cards of the same value are stacked on top of each other to show how many cards of that value are present on the table. Cards of different values are placed in numerical order forming a sequence on the table. The first player to play all the cards in their hand wins. How to Play The game consists of several rounds. Each round is divided into turns that proceed clockwise. On their turn, the active player, if they can and if they want, plays one or more cards of the same value from their hand. Multiple cards of the same value are stacked on top of each other to show how many cards of that value are present on the table. Cards of different values are placed in numerical order, forming a sequence on the table. Cards you can play The first player can play as many cards as they want of the same value. Subsequent players must play cards of the same value, following these rules: Cards with a lower or higher value Players can add cards of any value lower than the lowest card on the table or any value higher than the highest card. Played cards are placed to the left or right of the sequence on the table. Cards equal to the extremes Players can play cards that match the value of one of the last played cards on each end of the current sequence on the table. Played cards are stacked on those already present of the same value. The minimum number of cards Players must play a number of cards equal to or greater than the number of cards at the end of the sequence they are playing on (whether playing a lower/higher value or the same value as one of the ends). Intermediate values Players cannot play cards of any value between the two ends of the sequence on the table. Passing the turn If you cannot or do not want to play, you must pass. When you pass: Take one card of your choice from those visible on the table and add it to your hand. Note: This is an important choice: the card you take could be useful in the next round, but if you take a card from the ends of the sequence, you might help your opponents still playing in the current round. Turn your hand of cards face down. You are out of the current round and cannot play until the next round. End of the round The round ends when all players but one have passed. The last player who has not passed removes all cards face up on the table and becomes the first player of the new round. Like at the beginning of the game, they can play any cards they want and start a new sequence on the table. End of the game The game ends immediately when one player finishes the cards in their hand. Expert Variant This variant is designed for those who want to play a bit longer and adds a scoring system at the end of each game. How to Play Play a first game as explained above. [Rating: 2/10] Basically nothing new. A Frankenstein's creature made by assembling basic rules taken from other games.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA.  At least it's fast.  Shedding where you always play the middle cards first leaving very little room for choice.

[Rating: 4/10] Maybe it's better at higher player counts and if played aggressively?  My first game was pretty blah - had a great hand with doubles and triples and played out very quickly. If the other players had played low/high numbers after my plays perhaps they could have caused me troubles but not convinced that initial card draw doesn't have a significant effect on the outcome.

[Rating: 5/10] I'd like to play more to see the depths of it (if there is) but this is nice casual game so far

[Rating: 5/10] Interesting twist on a shedding game, where players are playing on either end (equal or higher than the highest card played, or equal or lower than the lowest card played, but you must also equal or exceed the # of already played on the end # you are playing on).  If you can't or don't want to play, you have to pass and pick up a card from those played, which might allow another player to play rather than pass.  Once you pass, you're out for the round. [Rating: 5/10] An okay card game with very low rules overhead. Fun to play for a little while, but it does wear out pretty quickly for me: there is not that much to see and explore from game to game. The amount of control you have in this game falls down the cliff very quickly, as soon as you add more players. To me it was best with 3p, but it can be enjoyable for couple of rounds with 4-5 too, just realize what you are in for.
